extracted.intended_audience: policy makers within DoD and the Marine Corps; Regional Contracting Officers assigned to Marine Corps installations
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and practical guidance for applying OMB Circular A-76 to competitive sourcing/outsourcing of installation support services in the Department of Defense, with emphasis on issues, risks, and lessons learned relevant to Marine Corps Regional Contracting Officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a function is inherently Governmental; such functions are "so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Governmental employees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision rests on factors including the level of governmental control, the ministerial nature of the function, and distinguishing between recurring operations and oversight. See OFPP guidance and Appendix C for lists of inherently governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Defense or Intelligence Security exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Services involving national defense or intelligence security are situations where cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the categories for which A-76 cost comparisons are exempt; treat as non-comparable under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Care exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient care services are excluded from cost comparisons and need not undergo A-76 cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized as an exemption category; these functions are treated separately from commercial activity competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Capability exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Capability — generally related to technical capabilities — is a category where cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity is classified as a core capability, it should not be subjected to A-76 cost comparison studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Development exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and Development activities are among the situations where cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat R&D functions as exempt from standard A-76 competitive sourcing cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: No satisfactory commercial source exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If no satisfactory commercial source is available, the function is exempt from a cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when market analysis shows insufficient or unacceptable private-sector capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-function (<=10 FTE) rule and 11+ FTE condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions with 10 or fewer Full Time Employees (FTE) do not require a cost comparison. For functions with 11 or more FTE a cost comparison is not needed if a fair and reasonable price can be obtained through competition and all affected Federal employees are reassigned to other comparable positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply thresholds when deciding whether to initiate an A-76 cost comparison; reassignment of personnel and ability to obtain fair price are key conditions for bypassing the formal cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current performance exceeds industry standards exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If current Government performance exceeds generally recognized industry performance and cost standards, a cost comparison is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performance and cost benchmarking to determine exemption; document evidence that government performance and cost are superior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary authorizations for in-house performance exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary authorizations for in-house performance are a category that does not require cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to short-term authorizations where formal A-76 comparisons would be impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a PWS that defines what is being requested, the performance standards and measures and timeframes of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must be performance-oriented, state outputs/measures and limiting directions, not indicate how a supplier should perform, and must ensure it does not limit service operations, arbitrarily increase risk, reduce competition, violate industry norms, or omit statutory/regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a QASP to describe methods of inspections to be used, the reports required and the resources to be expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP complements the PWS. It does not need to be published in the solicitation nor given to Government employees developing the management study. Competing sources are expected to develop their own Quality Assurance Plan based solely on the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance of a management study to determine the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a management study to determine the Government's MEO as the basis for the in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management Plan should reflect the scope of the PWS and identify organizational structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, inspection plans, and assumptions used to develop the MEO and in-house cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the in-house Government cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an in-house cost estimate based on the MEO and documented assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost estimate must be fair, accurate, and calculated in accordance with A-76 requirements; document assets, transition plan, QA plan and other assumptions supporting the estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of solicitation (RFP or IFB) per FAR and service regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue the Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB) through appropriate channels in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and other statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select IFB or RFP depending on nature of services. Treat proposals the same as other procurements concerning security, responsiveness, and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of in-house bid vs contract/ISSA price using Cost Comparison Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the in-house bid against the proposed contract or Inter-service Support Agreement (ISSA) price using the Cost Comparison Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sealed bids open all bids including in-house estimate and enter prices on the cost comparison form; announce tentative decision subject to evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility; for negotiated procurements, compare the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal against in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal process and protest resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an administrative appeal process to assure all costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form are fair, accurate and calculated in accordance with A-76, and resolve protests by unsuccessful offerors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final resolution of protests is an intrinsic part of A-76 competitions; contracting officers must follow established procedures but cannot eliminate the risk of protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy principle: Government should not compete with private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding policy: 'In the process of governing, the Government should not compete with its citizens' — the Government generally should rely on commercial sources for products and services it needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underpins A-76 and competitive sourcing initiatives; exceptions exist for inherently governmental functions and other statutory restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Federal Activities Inventory Reform (FAIR) Act, agency heads must submit a list of activities they believe are not inherently governmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAIR Act does not mandate outsourcing but creates inventories to identify commercial activities that could be considered for competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS drafting constraints to preserve competition and control risk
rubrics_metrics.description: When drafting the PWS ensure it 'does not limit service operations, arbitrarily increase risk, reduce competition, violate industry service or service group norms or omit statutory or regulatory requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly written PWSs are cited by GAO as a factor reducing projected savings; PWS clarity and correctness are critical to avoid later contract modifications and disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: QASP publication and use constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The QASP does not need to be published in the solicitation nor provided to government employees developing the management study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitors will develop their own QA plans based on the PWS; QASP documents how the government will inspect and verify performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan (MEO) documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management Plan must document best structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, inspection plans, and the assumptions used in developing the MEO and in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also must document assets of the organization, Quality Assurance Plan, Transition Plan and in-house cost estimate to support the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and mitigation for competitive sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify significant risk factors in contracting of services (e.g., mandated wage increases, poorly written PWS, contractor low-balling, deficiencies revealed during early contractor operations, contract modifications, and protests) and develop mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO and RAND studies highlight these risks; mitigation includes careful PWS/QASP drafting, realistic cost estimates, appropriate contract type selection, and lessons-learned systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lessons learned and a lessons-learned system
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and apply lessons learned from prior competitive sourcing activities and litigation to improve future A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO recommends a lessons-learned system to enhance the study process and reduce recurrence of known pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type selection to manage risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Select contract types (e.g., fixed-price, award-fee) appropriate to the risks inherent in the service being sourced, as contract type affects the nature and amount of risk the installation must accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contractor incentives, potential for low-balling, and potential need for price adjustments when choosing contract type; consider studies referenced (e.g., thesis work on award-fee suitability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of a common family of installation support services
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the nature and scope of installation support services that are being competitively sourced across DoD to establish a common family of services suitable for competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey and historical data (e.g., facilities maintenance, base operations, painting, plumbing) are used to identify recurring commercial activity groupings appropriate for A-76 competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing of competitive sourcing and source selection teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly staff the competitive sourcing team and the source selection team with qualified personnel to manage the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing affects study quality, risk management, and defensibility against protests; include contracting, technical, legal, and QA expertise as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of an acquisition strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an acquisition strategy that frames how the competition will be conducted, how risks will be managed, and how requirements will be procured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition strategy influences solicitation type, contract structure, market approach, and risk allocation; should be grounded in lessons learned and market analysis.
